text.p: The Turkish central bank injected a total of 34.5 trillion lira into a cash-strapped market via overnight lending and seven-day repos on Thursday.

It fed banks 8.5 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent on the interbank after buying 26 trillion lira of seven-day repos at an average rate of 74.74 percent on the open market, up slightly from 74.29 percent in Wednesday's eight-day repo auction.
The market had opened 57 trillion lira short, mainly due to banks' value-added tax payments to the Treasury.
Bankers said overnight rates went as high as 79 percent in the secondary money market amid fears the central bank would not meet all of the strong lira demand in the market.

"We believe that the central bank also intervened in the repo market in the afternoon to keep rising rates under control and feed more cash by buying repos. After that, overnight money rates eased in the secondary market," a banker said.
The Turkish lira closed weaker at 96,150 against the dollar, after Wednesday's 95,900 on a higher dollar/mark parity and the central bank's support for the U.S. currency.
The bank raised its key dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers to 96,050 lira from 96,000 at the opening and 95,750 at Wednesday's close.
T-bill yields increased across the board due to persisting liquidity shortage.
The average yield on the most heavily traded October 30, 1997 bond firmed to 117.84 percent from Wednesday's 117.50.
